answer:
DELIVERABLE — Qualifications for an Inspection Authorization (IA) with respect to MAJOR ALTERATIONS (14 CFR / FAA-AMT framework)

0. HOW THE QUESTION RESOLVES (read this first)
"Qualifications for inspection authorization regarding major alterations" is answered by TWO provisions, and any answer giving only one is wrong or incomplete:
  (A) ELIGIBILITY — 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)-(5): who may hold an IA at all. Note that the IA eligibility standard is itself written in terms of major alterations: the required written test is on returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations.
  (B) PER-ALTERATION AUTHORITY CONDITIONS — 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1): holding an IA is necessary but NOT sufficient; the alteration must have been accomplished in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator, and the aircraft must not be one maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program.
Controlling citation set (the answer): 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)-(5) + 65.95(a)(1), supported by 43.3, 43.5, 43.9, Part 1 §1.1, and Part 43 Appendix A.

"FAA-AMT" is read as the FAA aviation-maintenance-technician framework (mechanic certificate + IA). There is no separate AMT rule set that alters these requirements.

1. PART A — ELIGIBILITY TO HOLD AN IA: 14 CFR 65.91(c)
To be eligible for an inspection authorization, an applicant must satisfy ALL five elements:

| # | Element | Substance |
|---|---------|-----------|
| (c)(1) | Certificate/ratings | Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with BOTH an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective and in effect for a total of at least 3 years. |
| (c)(2) | Recent active experience | Actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the application date, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with 14 CFR. |
| (c)(3) | Fixed base of operations | A fixed base at which the applicant may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week; it need not be the place where the IA authority is exercised. |
| (c)(4) | Equipment, facilities, inspection data | Available equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance. |
| (c)(5) | Written test | Pass a written test on ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs AND major alterations, and for annual and progressive inspections under Part 43. |

Engineering reading of (c)(4) for the major-alteration case: "inspection data" must include the current type certificate data sheets/specifications, applicable airworthiness directives, the manufacturer's maintenance/overhaul data, and — critically — the Administrator-approved technical data for the specific alteration being inspected. An IA who does not hold the approved data for the alteration cannot satisfy (c)(4) as applied to that job.

2. PART B — CONDITIONS ON THE IA'S APPROVAL AFTER A MAJOR ALTERATION: 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1)
Quoted authority: the holder of an inspection authorization may "[i]nspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 of this chapter, if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator."

Four gates must all be satisfied before the IA signs:
  GATE 1 — CLASSIFICATION: the work is a major alteration (Part 1 §1.1; Part 43 Appendix A). If it is a minor alteration, §65.95(a)(1) is not the operative authority.
  GATE 2 — APPROVED DATA: the work was done in accordance with technical data APPROVED BY THE ADMINISTRATOR. The IA verifies against approved data; the IA does not create or approve that data (see §4 below).
  GATE 3 — AIRCRAFT EXCLUSION: the aircraft is not maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program (the parenthetical in §65.95(a)(1)).
  GATE 4 — RECORD/FORM: the §43.5(b) repair-or-alteration form (FAA Form 337) is executed as prescribed, the §43.9(a) maintenance record entry is made, and any changed operating limitations/flight data in the approved flight manual are revised per §43.5(c) and §91.9.

Related limit (why an A&P alone cannot do this): 14 CFR 43.3 provides that the maintenance authority it grants "does not authorize the performance of any inspection required by Part 91 or Part 125 of this chapter or any inspection performed after a major repair or alteration." So the post-major-alteration inspection/approval is IA work, not mechanic-certificate work.

3. GATE 1 DETAIL — WHAT MAKES IT "MAJOR"
Part 1 §1.1 defines a major alteration as an alteration not listed in the aircraft, aircraft engine, or propeller specifications that (1) might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness, or (2) is not done according to accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations. Part 43 Appendix A lists the enumerated major alteration categories by airframe, powerplant, propeller, and appliance, alongside the major repair and preventive maintenance lists. The Appendix A listing controls over colloquial usage; document the classification determination in the work package.

4. GATE 2 DETAIL — "APPROVED" vs "ACCEPTABLE" DATA (the most common compliance failure)
Approved data for a major alteration includes, for example: data approved as part of a type design (TC/ATC amendment), a supplemental type certificate (STC), data approved by the FAA as part of a field approval, and data approved by a properly delegated designee/ODA within the scope of that delegation. Guidance-type material (e.g., the AC 43.13-2 series "Acceptable Methods, Techniques, and Practices — Aircraft Alterations") is ACCEPTABLE data, not APPROVED data, and by itself does not support approval of a major alteration for return to service. An IA cannot self-approve alteration data and cannot substitute engineering judgment for approved data. VERIFY the current status/version of the AC 43.13-2, AC 43.9-1 (Form 337 completion) and AC 43-210 series (field approval/data approval) documents before citing them in a work package.

5. GATE 4 DETAIL — RECORDS AND FORM
- §43.5(b): no person may approve for return to service an aircraft/airframe/engine/propeller/appliance that has undergone a major repair or alteration unless the repair-or-alteration form authorized or furnished by the Administrator (FAA Form 337) has been executed in the manner prescribed by the Administrator.
- §43.9(a): maintenance record entry — description of work, date, name of the person performing the work, and the certificate number, plus reference to the approved data used.
- §43.5(c)/§91.9: if the alteration changes operating limitations or flight data in the approved flight manual, those must be revised and set forth as prescribed.
- VERIFY the current disposition/submission instructions for the executed Form 337 (the 48-hour submission practice is a form/AC instruction, not something quoted in the grounded text here).

6. CONTINUING QUALIFICATION (do not conflate with initial eligibility)
An IA is time-limited and must be renewed, so "qualified" is a continuing status: §65.92 sets the duration (each inspection authorization expires March 31 of each odd-numbered year, i.e., a 2-year term), and §65.93 governs renewal, requiring evidence that the applicant still meets §65.91(c)(1)-(4) plus satisfaction of defined recent-activity and/or refresher-training options during the period the authorization was held. VERIFY the exact §65.92/§65.93 wording and current activity/training options in the current eCFR text before relying on any specific option or hour count; the precise figures are deliberately not stated here because they were not verified.

7. PROCEDURE — PER-ALTERATION COMPLIANCE CHECKLIST FOR THE IA
Apply in order; any "NO" stops the sign-off.
1. Is the IA currently effective (not expired under §65.92, renewal current under §65.93)? [NO → stop]
2. Is the item classified as a major alteration under Part 1 §1.1 / Part 43 App A? [NO → use minor-alteration/§43.9 path, not §65.95(a)(1)]
3. Is the aircraft excluded by the §65.95(a)(1) Part 121 parenthetical? [YES → stop; IA authority does not extend]
4. Is there written technical data approved by the Administrator covering exactly this alteration on this make/model/serial? [NO → stop; obtain approved data (field approval/designee) before work or before approval]
5. Was the alteration physically accomplished in conformity with that approved data (conformity inspection complete)? [NO → stop; discrepancy must be resolved]
6. Are weight & balance, structural, electrical load, and systems effects accounted for per the approved data?
7. Are AFM supplements/operating limitations revisions required, and are they issued (§43.5(c)/§91.9)?
8. Execute FAA Form 337 (§43.5(b)) and the §43.9(a) record entry; return to service signed by the IA under §65.95(a)(1).

8. WORKED DETERMINATIONS
Case A — Wingtip LED recognition light installed under an FAA STC on a Part 91 Cessna 172. Major (electrical/structural change) → Gate 1 met. Data = STC = approved → Gate 2 met. Not Part 121 → Gate 3 met. Result: the IA may inspect and approve for return to service; execute Form 337 referencing the STC, record per §43.9(a), confirm W&B and any AFM/limitations changes.
Case B — Owner-fabricated bracket with no drawings, IA has only AC 43.13-2B-type guidance. Major (appreciably affects structural strength) → Gate 1 met, but Gate 2 FAILS: no Administrator-approved data. Result: the IA may NOT approve for return to service. Approved data must first be obtained (FAA field approval with designee/FAA engineering, or DER/ODA-approved data within delegation) and the article then shown to conform.
Case C — Same alteration on an aircraft maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program. Gate 3 FAILS: §65.95(a)(1) excludes it; approval must come through the operator's/duly authorized Part 121 program channels.

9. FAILURE MODES TO AUDIT FOR
- Treating the IA as authority to approve DATA (i.e., self-approving a field approval). It is not; the IA only approves the ARTICLE for return to service against already-approved data.
- Approving a major alteration on "acceptable" data or on engineering judgment alone.
- Signing on a Part 121 continuous-airworthiness aircraft.
- Missing the Form 337 / §43.9 entry / AFM-limitations revision.
- Confusing §65.95(a)(1) alteration authority with annual/progressive inspection authority under §65.95(a)(2).
- Signing with an expired authorization (post-March 31 of an odd-numbered year without renewal).
- Assuming the regulation imposes an airframe/powerplant category-class restriction on §65.95(a)(1): the text does not. Conversely, assuming there is no competence expectation at all: the IA remains responsible for being competent on the specific article; consult current FAA guidance before relying on any stated competence limitation.

10. CITATIONS (as retrieved; eCFR is the primary source)
- 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)-(5) — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.91 (quoted verbatim: the five eligibility elements, including the (c)(5) written test on returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations).
- 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1) — https://ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.95 (quoted verbatim: inspect/approve after major repair or major alteration if done per technical data approved by the Administrator; Part 121 parenthetical).

11. ASSUMPTIONS AND OPEN VERIFICATION ITEMS
